name: Hillel
title: Junior Temple Scribe
description: A young, meticulous scribe assigned to the Temple's administrative offices. Hillel is responsible for cross-referencing market ledgers for Passover lambs with the priestly inspection records. He is a man of data and process, but his work has led him to see a pattern in the week's events that transcends his ledgers.

attitude.neutral: Professional, precise, and focused on the details of the Law and Temple process.
attitude.positive: Becomes animated and insightful when he explains the connection between the lamb selection process and Jesus's movements.
attitude.negative: Is cautious and hesitant to speak too openly, aware that his conclusions could be seen as heretical by his superiors.

background: As a junior scribe, Hillel is not part of the high-level political maneuvering of the Sanhedrin. His perspective is grounded in the day-to-day logistics of the Passover festival, which gives him a unique, data-driven insight into the typological fulfillment of the Passover Lamb.
